title: QC limit
purpose: Add or edit inclusive acceptance bounds for one test definition, QC phase, QC type and measured/calculated quantity.
summary: Add or edit the acceptance bounds for one test, QC phase, QC type and measure. Only administrators can save; other staff read these values on QC configuration.

tasks.title: Add a QC limit
steps: Enter the [[Lower]] bound, the [[Upper]] bound or both.

tasks.title: Change a QC limit
steps: Open it from QC configuration and change the values.
Explain why in [[Reason for change]] and select [[Save changes]].

tasks.title: Stop using a QC limit without deleting it
steps: Clear [[Is active]], give a reason and select [[Save changes]]. The row and its history stay.

good_to_know: Bounds are inclusive. Measured value uses the result unit; recovery and RPD use percent.
A matrix spike duplicate needs both a recovery limit and an RPD limit.
A method blank reported as ND passes only against an upper bound.
Changing a limit re-evaluates current QC and can create or lift a hold. Approved results keep the evidence they relied on.

sections.title: Create, edit and access
paragraphs: Only administrators can open and save this form; other staff read these values on the QC configuration page, where the rows are not links for them. Add creates a new configuration record; Edit prepopulates the existing record and requires a Reason for change. Unknown configuration kinds are unavailable. These are lab policy values, and synthetic seed data is not a validated set.

items.label: Definition
items.description: Required exact method/version, analyte and matrix. Choices include catalog definitions ordered by method, analyte and matrix; this is not a limit for every analyte in a method.

items.label: Phase
items.description: Required Analysis (initial Add default) or Preparation. Keeps analytical QC limits separate from independent preparation QC limits.

items.label: Qc type
items.description: Required Method blank, Laboratory control sample, Matrix spike, Matrix spike duplicate, Laboratory duplicate or Calibration verification.

items.label: Measure
items.description: Required Measured value, Percent recovery or Relative percent difference. Choose the quantity this QC type actually evaluates.

items.label: Lower
items.description: Optional inclusive lower bound. Uses result unit for Measured value and percent for recovery/RPD. Decimal field supports up to 10 decimal places and 24 total digits.

items.label: Upper
items.description: Optional inclusive upper bound in the same quantity/unit. At least one bound must be supplied; lower cannot exceed upper.

items.label: Basis
items.description: Optional method/SOP reference for the bounds and applicability.

items.label: Is active
items.description: Initially checked. Current QC evaluation uses only active limits; deactivating does not create an assumed pass.

sections.title: Applicability and current evaluation
paragraphs: Only one limit row can exist for a definition, phase, QC type and measure, including inactive rows. An unrelated measure does not replace a required applicable measure. All applicable quantities need active bounds; missing ones produce Not evaluated and hold approval.

Current measurements are reevaluated under current limits. Changing a limit can restore or create a hold and invalidate the context of a prior accepted disposition. Approved result QC evidence and issued report snapshots remain historical records rather than being rewritten.

items.label: Method blank
items.description: Uses Measured value. For ND, a configured upper bound is essential: the applied reporting limit must be no greater than that bound.

items.label: Matrix spike
items.description: Uses Percent recovery with the native sample result subtracted.

items.label: Matrix spike duplicate
items.description: Requires both Percent recovery and Relative percent difference limits.

items.label: Add QC limit
items.description: Validate bounds and uniqueness, create the audited limit and return to QC configuration.

sections.title: Save, cancel and history
paragraphs: Validation errors preserve entered form values. A stale record is refused rather than overwriting another person’s edit; input stays visible, but reload and compare current values before saving again. A reload is a new form, so retain any needed unsaved notes before leaving.

items.label: Reason for change
items.description: Optional on creation; required nonblank for every existing-row save. Recorded with actor, time and before/after values.

items.label: Save changes
items.description: For an edit, validate fields and uniqueness, recheck that the record still matches the version opened, and save with its audit event. The Add form’s named submit button creates instead. Success returns to QC configuration.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Return to QC configuration without saving typed changes.

items.label: History
items.description: Existing records show their latest 20 audit events, displayed oldest to newest, with action, actor, time and reason. No history section appears before any events exist.
